title: Digital clock widget shows text in English regardless of the configured time locale
line: The clock's calendar now shows month and weekday names in your time format language instead of the interface language.
explanation: The calendar component deliberately took month and weekday names from the first UI language (a choice made for bug 353715), while the panel clock, its tooltip and the day numbering follow LC_TIME. With an English interface and a French time locale the popup therefore said 'November' and 'Mon Tue' next to a French tooltip and a Monday-first week. The change makes Calendar::monthName() and the QML weekday and month headers use the system locale, which takes names from LC_TIME, so the popup matches the clock.

commits.message:
components/calendar: Use the time locale for month and day names

The calendar took month and weekday names from the first UI language, so
with an English interface and a French time locale it showed English
names while the clock and its tooltip were French. Use LC_TIME instead.

BUG: 517822

patches.diff:
From 09b3686efac4604b7d299f109d737007d3b8116c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:37:25 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] components/calendar: Use the time locale for month and day
 names

The calendar took month and weekday names from the first UI language, so
with an English interface and a French time locale it showed English
names while the clock and its tooltip were French. Use LC_TIME instead.

BUG: 517822
---
 components/calendar/calendar.cpp         | 16 +---------------
 components/calendar/qml/DaysCalendar.qml |  2 +-
 components/calendar/qml/MonthView.qml    |  2 +-
 3 files changed, 3 insertions(+), 17 deletions(-)

diff --git a/components/calendar/calendar.cpp b/components/calendar/calendar.cpp
index 37e5c9e43e..6c7671f738 100644
--- a/components/calendar/calendar.cpp
+++ b/components/calendar/calendar.cpp
@@ -224,21 +224,7 @@ QString Calendar::dayName(int weekday) const
 
 QString Calendar::monthName() const
 {
-    // Simple QDate::longMonthName won't do the job as it
-    // will return the month name using LC_DATE locale which is used
-    // for date formatting etc. So for example, in en_US locale
-    // and cs_CZ LC_DATE, it would return Czech month names while
-    // it should return English ones. So here we force the LANG
-    // locale and take the month name from that.
-    //
-    // See https://bugs.kde.org/show_bug.cgi?id=353715
-
-    QLocale langLocale;
-
-    if (QLocale().uiLanguages().length() > 0) {
-        langLocale = QLocale(QLocale().uiLanguages().at(0));
-    }
-    return langLocale.standaloneMonthName(d->displayedDate.month());
+    return QLocale::system().standaloneMonthName(d->displayedDate.month());
 }
 
 int Calendar::year() const
diff --git a/components/calendar/qml/DaysCalendar.qml b/components/calendar/qml/DaysCalendar.qml
index 79be5996c2..55a108aad4 100644
--- a/components/calendar/qml/DaysCalendar.qml
+++ b/components/calendar/qml/DaysCalendar.qml
@@ -134,7 +134,7 @@ Item {
 
                 width: daysCalendar.cellWidth
                 height: daysCalendar.cellHeight
-                text: Qt.locale(Qt.locale().uiLanguages[0]).dayName(((daysCalendar.backend.firstDayOfWeek + index) % dayOfWeekHeaderRepeater.count), Locale.ShortFormat)
+                text: Qt.locale().dayName(((daysCalendar.backend.firstDayOfWeek + index) % dayOfWeekHeaderRepeater.count), Locale.ShortFormat)
                 textFormat: Text.PlainText
                 level: 2
                 type: Kirigami.Heading.Type.Primary
diff --git a/components/calendar/qml/MonthView.qml b/components/calendar/qml/MonthView.qml
index 619852a770..80ce8fe8a3 100644
--- a/components/calendar/qml/MonthView.qml
+++ b/components/calendar/qml/MonthView.qml
@@ -228,7 +228,7 @@ Item {
         Component.onCompleted: {
             for (let i = 0; i < 12; ++i) {
                 append({
-                    label: Qt.locale(Qt.locale().uiLanguages[0]).standaloneMonthName(i, Locale.LongFormat),
+                    label: Qt.locale().standaloneMonthName(i, Locale.LongFormat),
                     monthNumber: i + 1,
                     yearNumber: 2050,
                     isCurrent: true,
--

Same setup with the fix: 'Novembre' and 'lun. mar. mer. ...'

review.text: This patch silently reverts an intentional, documented fix for bug 353715 (which ensured English-UI users with a regional LC_TIME for 24h/Monday-first formatting still saw English month and weekday names instead of a mixed-language popup) without even mentioning 353715 in the commit message. Worse, unconditionally switching from uiLanguages[0] to QLocale::system()/Qt.locale() introduces an i18n regression on Plasma setups where only Language (LANGUAGE) is changed in Region & Language while LANG remains en_US and LC_TIME is unset, because QLocale::system() ignores LANGUAGE and falls back to LANG. Because bugs 353715 and 517822 directly contradict each other, this needs an explicit maintainer/VDG decision rather than blindly overturning 353715.
changes: Get maintainer/VDG agreement on whether calendar month/weekday names should follow LC_TIME (overturning bug 353715) or UI language (in which case the digital clock tooltip/panel should be made consistent with UI language instead).
If LC_TIME is chosen, avoid breaking LANGUAGE != LANG setups when LC_TIME is not explicitly overridden, and explicitly document the intentional reversal of bug 353715 in the commit message.

reviews.text: The code is right and small. Calendar::monthName() and the QML weekday and month headers now use the LC_TIME locale, which makes them consistent with Calendar::dayName() (already QLocale::system()), the panel clock, the tooltip and the first day of the week. The screenshots show French names with LC_TIME=fr_FR and English names when LC_TIME is unset. But this deliberately reverses the behaviour added for bug 353715, and the commit message says nothing about it, so a reviewer will ask why the old choice is being undone. Users who set LC_TIME only to get 24-hour or ISO formats will now see month and day names in that language.
changes: Mention in the commit message that this reverses the bug 353715 behaviour (add CCBUG: 353715) and give the consistency argument: the clock, the tooltip, dayName() and the first day of the week already follow LC_TIME.
Raise the 353715 trade-off in the MR description so the digital-clock and calendar maintainers explicitly make the product decision.
